chunks.label: And then
chunks.rationale: Lets you tell what happened next in a story.
chunks.interference: Soshite sounds tidy; in chat sore kara is more natural, and soshitara often signals a surprise.

chunks.label: Adding and choosing
chunks.rationale: Lets you add another point or offer a choice.
chunks.interference: Sore to (and also) and sore to mo (or) differ by one syllable.

chunks.label: Life, light, boats, visits
chunks.rationale: Four common words for life, light, travel by boat and going to see someone.
chunks.interference: Tazuneru (visit) sounds the same as tazuneru (ask).

chunks.label: Changing the subject
chunks.rationale: Lets you switch topics or slip in a side fact.
chunks.interference: Tokoro de opens a new topic; chinami ni adds a side fact on the same one.

chunks.label: Even so and but
chunks.rationale: Lets you push back, add a caveat or set a condition.
chunks.interference: Sore demo (even so) vs sore de (so); dakara tte (just because) vs dakara (so).

chunks.label: Sleep and tiredness
chunks.rationale: Lets you say how you slept and how tired you are.
chunks.interference: Utouto is light dozing, gussuri deep sleep; furafura is dizzy, kutakuta worn out.

chunks.label: Hunger, thirst and aches
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe hunger, thirst, nausea, pain and shivering.

chunks.label: Warm, muggy, rainy weather
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about warm, damp and rainy days.
chunks.interference: Mushimushi is hot and muggy; jimejime is damp.

chunks.label: Lazing and wandering
chunks.rationale: Lets you say you lazed around or wandered about.
chunks.interference: Burabura is strolling for fun; urouro is aimless or suspicious.

chunks.label: Moods at a glance
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe a mood you can see or feel.
chunks.interference: Moyamoya (nagging unease) and bootto (blank mind) both sound vague but differ.

chunks.label: How well it's done
chunks.rationale: Lets you say how well, how roughly or how steadily something is done.

chunks.label: Empty, packed, messy
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe crowded, empty and messy places.

chunks.label: Food textures
chunks.rationale: Lets you praise food by its texture.
chunks.interference: Sakusaku is light and airy-crisp, paripari thin and snappy.

chunks.label: Surfaces and wetness
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe how things look and feel to the touch.
chunks.interference: Sarasara is dry-smooth; tsurutsuru is slick or slippery.

chunks.label: Reasons and conclusions
chunks.rationale: Lets you get to the root of things and draw conclusions.
chunks.interference: Dakara koso (exactly why) vs dakara tte (just because ... doesn't mean).

chunks.label: Rephrasing and hedging
chunks.rationale: Lets you correct yourself, flip an expectation or hedge.
chunks.interference: Mushiro picks the better of two options; gyaku ni flips an expectation.

drops.reason: Duplicates それより (same meaning with emphatic mo); covered in its notes.
